facts.statement: Sefapanosaurus is a genus of dinosaur.
facts.quote: taxon: Sefapanosaurus

facts.statement: The genus Sefapanosaurus was described by Otero and colleagues in 2015.
facts.quote: authority: Otero et al., 2015

facts.statement: Fossils of Sefapanosaurus date to the Early Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Jurassic

facts.statement: Sefapanosaurus was an early herbivorous sauropodomorph that lived in southern Gondwana approximately 200 million years ago during the Late Triassic or Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: Sefapanosaurus was an early, herbivorous sauropodomorph dinosaur occurring in the southern regions of Gondwana some 200 million years ago in the Late Triassic or Early Jurassic.

facts.statement: A distinctive anatomical feature of Sefapanosaurus is a cross-shaped astragalus bone in its ankle.
facts.quote: A distinctive feature of this dinosaur is the cross-shaped astragalus or talus bone in its ankle.

facts.statement: The generic name Sefapanosaurus combines the Sesotho word for 'cross' and the Greek word for 'lizard'.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Sesotho word sefapano, meaning 'cross' and the Greek word saurus, meaning 'lizard'.

facts.statement: The specific name zastronensis refers to Zastron, the location where the type specimen was found.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to Zastron, the type locality, where the specimen was discovered.

facts.statement: Sefapanosaurus was formally described in the June 23, 2015 issue of the Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society.
facts.quote: This new genus was described in the 23 June 2015 issue of 'Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society'

facts.statement: Fossils of Sefapanosaurus, including a partial left foot and four partial skeletons, were excavated from the Elliot Formation in the Zastron district of South Africa in the late 1930s.
facts.quote: A portion of the left foot and four partial skeletons, including several pieces of spine and limbs, were excavated from the Elliot Formation in the late 1930s in the Zastron district in South Africa, some 30 km from the Lesotho border.

facts.statement: Before recent study, the Sefapanosaurus fossils were part of the collection at the Evolutionary Studies Institute at Wits University.
facts.quote: Until a few years ago these formed part of the large fossil collection curated by the Evolutionary Studies Institute (ESI) at Wits University.

facts.statement: Further analysis revealed that the remains represented a new genus intermediate between early bipedal sauropodomorphs and later giant quadrupedal sauropods.
facts.quote: Further study determined that the remains represented a new dinosaur genus which was intermediate between early bipedal sauropodomorphs and the later giant quadruped sauropods

facts.statement: Sefapanosaurus belongs to the order Saurischia.
facts.quote: ordo: Saurischia

facts.statement: Sefapanosaurus is classified within the suborder Sauropodomorpha.
facts.quote: subordo: Sauropodomorpha

facts.statement: The binomial name Sefapanosaurus zastronensis was established by Otero, Krupandan, Pol, Chinsamy, Choinier, and colleagues in 2015.
facts.quote: binomial_authority: Otero, Krupandan, Pol, Chinsamy y Choinier et al., 2015

facts.statement: Sefapanosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic, specifically the Pliensbachian stage, approximately 200 million years ago in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 200 millones de años, durante el Pliensbachiano, en lo que es hoy África.

facts.statement: Sefapanosaurus was one of the first herbivorous sauropodomorph dinosaurs to live in the southern regions of Gondwana.
facts.quote: Fue uno de los primeros dinosaurios sauropodomorfos herbívoros que vivieron en las regiones del sur de Gondwana.

facts.statement: The fossils of Sefapanosaurus were initially thought to belong to the genus Aardonyx.
facts.quote: Inicialmente se pensaba que los restos eran de Aardonyx.

facts.statement: Sefapanosaurus is considered a transitional genus between bipedal sauropodomorphs and giant quadrupedal sauropods.
facts.quote: se descubrió que era un nuevo género intermedio entre los sauropodomorfos bípedos y los saurópodos gigantes cuadrúpedos

facts.statement: The time range for Sefapanosaurus is estimated from 227.3 to 199.5 million years ago, spanning the Norian and Hettangian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Hettangian (227.3 to 199.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Sefapanosaurus is grouped within the Sauropodiformes.
facts.quote: Parent group: Sauropodiformes
